gap: No result ChatGPT got states a figure anyone measured or observed in use: the only named field numbers are Jules Whicker's (Shooting Times, 7 July 2026) for the DJI Matrice 4T, who identifies deer at 200 m to 400 m and expects 30 to 45 minutes per charge against the 49 minutes DJI rates.
standout_why: Compared against blog.dronetrader.com/thermal-drones-for-sale, nighthunting.net/thermal-drones, bestthermaldrone.com/best-thermal-drones and bestthermaldrone.com/compare (B&H compare pages are maker spec grids and were not opened). None carries a tested figure: nighthunting says its distances are 'calculated from the sensor and lens', bestthermaldrone says 'Spec score from published specs, not a test', and dronetrader checked only prices. So the angle is new against all of them, but it is thin. The one solid named reviewer covers the Matrice 4T, which Dealectric does not list. The only hands-on numbers for the Autel EVO Lite 640T and EVO II Dual 640T V3 come from an Amazon-affiliate listicle with no instruments or method. No lab (RTINGS-style) measurement was found for any candidate. A side-by-side of EU declared sound power levels would lift this to 2, but I could not read the declarations.
decides: It does not change the pick. It supports a caution that applies to every candidate: plan on less than the rated flight time (Whicker's 30 to 45 minutes is 61% to 92% of DJI's 49; the Autel hands-on figures are about 95% of rating). Whicker's 1,500 m detect versus 200 m to 400 m identify gap on the Matrice 4T is the most useful number for a wildlife shopper. The Matrice 4T has a 7x tele camera to do that identifying; whether the cheaper Autel EVO Lite 640T ($3,359) can identify at similar range has no measured answer.
